main_body: Open wooden weapon rack: two side posts, a top beam, a mid rail and a base beam, holding four weapons (axe, mace, halberd, sword) upright.
top_band: Light tan band on the top beam, rows 9-11 (about 3 rows). A similar light band sits on the base beam at rows 26-28.
evidence: In a column through the top beam I read a light tan top (rows 9-11), a step to mid brown, then a darker front face (rows 12-14). The base beam repeats this: a light top at rows 26-28 with a dark front below at rows 29-30. The beam tops read as horizontal surfaces, as the frame kind requires. The mid rail's top is thin, but the main beams show clear top faces. The posts and weapons are vertical, as expected for a frame.

style.evidence: The wood has about 3-4 steps (light top, mid, dark front, deep shadow), and the dark outlines lean brown, so they are material-toned rather than black. The posts, the weapon shafts and the beam fronts are flat, grain-free fills of one colour. The metal blades have 2-3 grey steps and the red-orange mace heads are flat. The pieces are simple next to the well and the stall, which carry per-stone shading, tile scallops and more texture per tile. This reads thinner and flatter than the reference.
